newsitem.title: USA: China MFN a "$4 bln vote" for US farmers-Glickman.
newsitem.headline: China MFN a "$4 bln vote" for US farmers-Glickman.

text.p: Farm-state U.S. senators, a friendly audience for Clinton administration arguments for renewal of Most Favored Nation (MFN) trade status for China, said Wednesday that China must agree to abide by world trade rules.
The U.S. House (of Representatives) was expected to vote next week on renewing MFN for one year for China.
"To American agriculture, this could be a minimum $4 billion vote," Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said during a Senate Agriculture Committee hearing.
Without MFN, he said, China could turn to other exporter nations for cotton, grain and meat, he said.
Members of the committee generally indicated their support for China MFN and focused on a related trade issue -- China's desire to join the World Trade Organization.

Senators urged Glickman and U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky to require China to settle its outstanding farm trade disputes and to agree to follow world trade rules as a condition of joining WTO.

"With China going into WTO, these things have to be worked out in advance,' said Senator Charles Grassley, Iowa Republican. "If we don't do it, China will be our biggest competitor, instead of our biggest customer."
"We will not conclude our WTO negotiations with China without receiving solid, commercially meaningful commitments on agriculture," Barshefsky said.
Several disputes handicap Sino-U.S. trade. The most prominent was China's refusal to buy wheat from the Pacific Northwest on grounds it might contain the TCK smut fungus.
"Of all the ag issues, on this they are the most intransigent," Barshefsky said.
"They've got a brain lock. It's amazing," said Senator Larry Craig, Idaho Republican.
